description: B2 English — second and third conditionals, hypothetical scenarios

diarizedTranscript.speaker: tutor
diarizedTranscript.text: Hi Lucia. Today: second and third conditionals. Hypotheticals.

diarizedTranscript.speaker: student
diarizedTranscript.text: Okay. The second is for unreal present, right? If I had money I would travel.

diarizedTranscript.speaker: tutor
diarizedTranscript.text: Exactly. And third is for unreal past. If I had studied medicine, I would have become a doctor.

diarizedTranscript.speaker: student
diarizedTranscript.text: Got it. If I had studied earlier, I would pass the exam.

diarizedTranscript.speaker: tutor
diarizedTranscript.text: Mix-up: that's mixing second and third. Either 'I would have passed' (third, past consequence) or 'if I studied earlier I would pass' (second, present pattern).

diarizedTranscript.speaker: student
diarizedTranscript.text: Right. If I had studied earlier, I would have passed the exam yesterday.

diarizedTranscript.speaker: tutor
diarizedTranscript.text: Perfect. Now you: imagine you won the lottery.

diarizedTranscript.speaker: student
diarizedTranscript.text: If I won the lottery, I would buy a house in Barcelona and quit my job.

diarizedTranscript.speaker: tutor
diarizedTranscript.text: Now mixed conditional: 'If I were richer (now), I would have bought that car (past)'.

diarizedTranscript.speaker: student
diarizedTranscript.text: If I were taller, I would have played basketball professionally.

diarizedTranscript.speaker: student
diarizedTranscript.text: Thanks. Conditionals make English feel philosophical.

diarizedTranscript.speaker: tutor
diarizedTranscript.text: True. Homework: write a short story using 5 conditionals — mix types.
